---
title: "Graywolf Container"
---

## Background

[Graywolf](https://github.com/chrissnell/graywolf) is an open-source APRS
(Automatic Packet Reporting System) station for amateur radio. It combines a
software modem (written in Rust, with AFSK demodulation ported from Dire Wolf),
an AX.25/APRS service (written in Go) that handles beaconing, digipeating and
iGate duties, and a web interface. It ships as a single binary plus a SQLite
configuration database, and can talk to radios through KISS and AGWPE over TCP.

This project packages graywolf as a container so it can be run, moved and
rebuilt with one or two `podman compose` commands instead of a hand-managed
install.

## What this container provides

- **Multi-architecture image.** The same `Containerfile` builds for `amd64`
  (PC, server) and `arm64` (Raspberry Pi 5). It installs the official graywolf
  release and verifies it against the published checksums.
- **Two ways to run it:**
  - **Standalone (APRS-IS only).** No radio hardware; the container connects
    to the APRS-IS network for simple monitoring.
  - **With a Digirig.** A [Digirig](https://digirig.net) USB interface is
    passed into the container: its sound card for audio and its serial port for
    PTT (push-to-talk) via RTS/DTR.
- **Saved run rules.** Compose files capture the ports, volume and device
  passthrough, so nothing has to be remembered or retyped.
- **Persistent data.** Configuration and packet history are kept in
  `./graywolf-data/`, outside the container, so rebuilding the image does not
  lose your station setup.

| File                   | Purpose                                         |
|------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| `Containerfile`        | Builds the image for amd64 or arm64             |
| `compose.yaml`         | Base service: web UI on port 8080, no radio     |
| `compose.digirig.yaml` | Overlay adding Digirig audio and serial devices |

## Quick start

```bash
podman compose up -d --build        # no radio, APRS-IS only
```

Then open <http://localhost:8080> to configure graywolf.

For the Digirig overlay, host group requirements and troubleshooting, see
[Building and running](usage.qmd).
